text: If the doctor has been killed, why would the murderer stay in his room, asked Utterson, who thought the story too wild to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole explained that for a whole week the thing in the cabinet had been crying out night and day for some kind of medicine. <break time="0.8s" /> It threw written orders onto the stairs, and Poole had been sent to every chemist in London, only to have the drug returned as impure. <break time="0.8s" /> He showed one of the notes, which was in the doctors handwriting and ended, For Gods sake, find me some of the old. <break time="0.8s" /> This is certainly the doctors hand, said Utterson, but Poole cried, What does the handwriting matter, sir, I have seen him. <break time="0.8s" /> He had come into the laboratory one day and found the creature digging among the boxes, with a mask over its face. <break time="0.8s" /> The moment it saw him, it gave a cry like a rat and ran upstairs, and Pooles hair stood on end with fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson suggested that the doctor had a terrible illness, one that changed his looks and voice and made him hide behind a mask. <break time="0.8s" /> But Poole disagreed, for his master was tall and well built, while the thing he had seen was more like a dwarf.
